[[File:Allium-polyanthum-inflo.jpg|thumb|left|200px]]
'''''Allium polyanthum''''', called the '''many-flowered garlic''', is a [[Mediterranean]] species of [[wild onion]] native to [[Spain]], [[France]], [[Italy]], [[Morocco]], and [[Tunisia]].<ref name=juanita>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=296299 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref> It is widely cultivated for its edible and potently aromatic bulbs and foliage.<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=allium+polyanthum Altervista Flora Italiana, Aglio con molti fiori, ''Allium polyanthum'']</ref>

''Allium polyanthum'' produces an egg-shaped bulb, often with small [[bulblet]]s around the base. [[Scape (botany)|Scape]] can be up to 80 cm tall. Leaves are flat and broadly linear, tapering at the tip. Flowers are numerous and small, white or pink.<ref>Josef August Schultes & Julius Hermann Schultes. 1830. Systema vegetabilium: secundum classes, ordines, genera, species. Cum characteribus differentiis et synonymis. Editio nova, speciebus inde ab editione XV. Detectis aucta et locupletata. Stuttgardtiae 7(2): 1016.</ref><ref>O.Bolòs & al. 1990.  Flora Manual del Països Catalans 1213, ''Allium ampeloprasum'' subsp. ''polyanthum''</ref><ref>Jauzein, Philippe & Tison, J.-M. 2005.Lejeunia n.s., 178: 12, ''Allium porrum'' subsp. ''polyanthum''</ref>
